newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech FinMin to choose IPB adviser soon.
newsitem.headline: Czech FinMin to choose IPB adviser soon.

text.p: A senior Czech Finance Ministry official said the financial adviser to the sale of some 36 percent of IPB a.s bank will be chosen soon but declined comment on a report that Salomon Brothers would be selected.

"A decision will be taken soon and soon means in the next couple of days but who is going to chosen, I really cannot say," Pavel Stepanek, head of the ministry's financial markets policy division, told Reuters.
The Hospodarske Noviny business daily, citing "a highly reputable source" reported that Salomon would be chosen to advise on the sale and that talks were focused on the level of fees.
"We have no comment to make on that report," a Salomon spokeswoman said in London.
Stepanek said the entire state stake would be sold off.
The government holds 31.5 percent through the National Property Fund (NPF) and some five percent through the Ceska Posta postal service.
"The government has decided that this would be sold altogether," Stepanek said. Other details of the sell-off have not been revealed.
Asked about the timetable for the sale, Stepanek said, "Within the framework of transparency, it should be as quick as possible."
The IPB stake sell-off is the first step in the government's aim to fully privatise its stakes in the four laragest Czech banks, although plans for the other three have yet to be agreed.
A special committee has been formed at the Finance Ministry to prepare the sale, which is expected to be geared toward choosing a strong foreign partner.
A senior economic aide to Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said in November that Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) was seeking to be the arranger for the sale.
NPF chairman Roman Ceska, who does not have a seat in the cabinet which must approve the sale, has said Japanese investment bank Nomura has the "best chance" to win the tender.
Czech media have also said Dutch ING Groep NV and ABN AMRO as parties are interested in taking a stake in IPB, although both have refused to comment on the matter.
